s1.syndrome_frame: A middle-aged woman with a history of cancer presenting with a new onset of neurological symptoms and a mass lesion in the brain
salient_findings: Mass lesion in the right temporal lobe
key_facts: 46-year-old Japanese woman
History of epilepsy
History of breast cancer
Redness and swelling of the right breast
Erythema and swelling in the lower right breast
Ultrasound revealed a low-echo mass with partially unclear margins
Biopsy showed invasive ductal carcinoma
High grade, ER+, PgR–, HER2 3+, Ki67 70%
Whole-body PET-CT revealed increased uptake in multiple areas
Received FEC chemotherapy and trastuzumab plus pertuzumab with docetaxel
Achieved clinical complete response for 23 months
Developed persistent headache two years after treatment initiation
CT and MRI of the head revealed a 30-mm mass lesion in the right temporal lobe

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of stage IV breast cancer with multiple metastases and achieved a clinical complete response for 23 months before developing a persistent headache and a mass lesion in the right temporal lobe, which is consistent with brain metastasis from breast cancer.

rejected.label: Glioblastoma Multiforme
rejected.why: No prior evidence of primary brain tumor

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Typically a slow-growing tumor, inconsistent with rapid onset of symptoms

rejected.why: No prior evidence of primary brain tumor

rejected.label: Oligodendroglioma
rejected.why: No prior evidence of primary brain tumor

rejected.label: Cerebral Metastasis
rejected.why: Too general, as the patient has a known primary cancer

rejected.label: Breast Cancer Leptomeningeal Metastasis
rejected.why: The mass lesion is in the temporal lobe, not leptomeningeal
